# 2018 POWER UP – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27).

## Game play / meta
- The dominant factor was **early control of the scale, then keeping it on your side**. Once it tipped your way it
  was easier to keep stacking than when it tipped against you (you need to stack higher, which is especially hard
  when there are already a few layers of cubes). The scale was worth more points than anything else in the game.
- **254 took it to perfection with a consistent 4-cube AUTO**, kept its lead from that point, dominated the entire
  season and did not lose a single match (undefeated).
- Dominant game play: two robots on the scale in AUTO (the third on the switch). In TELEOP the top two focused on the
  scale; when needed, one went to the opponent's switch and the other to the near switch or the vault. The third
  robot played defense, the opponent's switch, or our vault/switch (or a combination).
- **Double climb**: either a buddy climb (the third robot climbs onto the top robot's passive forklift), or two top
  robots hook onto the rung with a rope and make room for each other to climb together (simple and effective).
- Dominant concept: **elevator with a wheeled gripper on a wrist** (placing on scale, switch and vault). Elite robots
  had very tall elevator reach (for a scale tipped against you plus stacking on top of 3 layers of cubes) and gentle
  placement. The elevator also served for the climb plus a passive forklift buddy climb, or a hook-and-release
  combined climb of two teammates (simpler, but both robots need it).
- In early quals, when weak teams did not have a drive-straight AUTO (an RP), **elite teams sent programmers to write
  their partners' AUTO before the match**.

## Dominant robots
- **254** – by far the best that season, and not that complex: a lift with a gripper on a wrist that intakes cubes
  from the floor, with V-shaped side wheels. It could eject with the wheels, or gently place by opening the V-wheel
  "claws" with a piston – gentle placement helped on a large pile of cubes already on the scale. For an effective
  vault, the gripper could turn 180° and they slid the cube through the robot into the vault (taking from the pyramid
  pile near the switch and putting into the vault without rotating the robot).
- Many other dominant robots followed 254's concept: 2910, 1323, 1678, 2481, 1619, 2122, 195, 2056.
- **2910** – singled out because it was a super simple robot and still one of the best despite all its design
  trade-offs: a 2-stage elevator, no pivot for the gripper end effector (so less reach), ground intake through a cut
  in the bumper with the end effector; climbed with the elevator directly (hook-and-release robots could climb with
  them). Very light with a low CoG, so the robot was very zippy, with a great driver.

## Effective mechanisms
- **254 / 1678 / 1323 gripper (end effector) on a pivot** – V-shaped compliant 2 in wheels, each side on a different
  motor so a cube taken diagonally can be rotated in; gentle release by opening the claw with a piston. 1574 had a nice
  version with grippy polycord instead of sets of wheels.
- **254 forklift** – passive forklift, opened once with a servo latch; carbon rods, so a small footprint that every
  robot could get onto.
- **254 / 1577 / 2056 forklift** – passive aluminium forklift; the meta buddy climb that year (maybe because 118
  released it first and everyone copied). The winch that pulls the robot up also tilts the forklift upward, so the
  partner robots do not slide off.
- **148 bumper grabber** – a shorter "forklift" with active velcro rollers that grab the partners' bumpers (they had to
  put velcro on their partners before the match).
- **254 / 2910** elevator.
- **2481 / 1678** over-the-back wrist, to place cubes the other way.
- **3538 sideways elevator** – the first introduction of a sideways elevator: an easy way to let a horizontal or
  sideways rotating arm on the elevator swing 180° without hitting the elevator (pass-through or over-the-back is
  still possible with regular elevators if the integration allows it).
- **195** tall elevator.
- **2122** semi-turreted end effector.
- **1574 buddy climb** – climb, and put an identical bar at the same height next to it to make room for partners.
- **1574** two pivoting arms instead of an elevator with a pivoting gripper (niche, not the meta).
- **7039** – single-stage elevator/rail: started collapsed to half height, opened once the match started, then stayed
  tall.
- **1619** wide cube gripper with two horizontal round tubes (upper and lower kickers).
- **971** – not dominant in this game, but inspired several 2023/2025 robots: a double-jointed arm (lower joint at the
  base) with roughly equal-length carbon-fiber links (the second slightly shorter) and a super-light end effector; the
  larger gearbox at the side of the robot; motion through steel cable or a thick timing belt.
- **610 / 4613** – low robots that launched cubes onto the scale: quick and effective to load the scale, but once it
  was stacked with cubes the shots could knock cubes off. Still effective on the switch and the vault.
